chapter: Alma Hightower and other women musicians
title: Hearing Hightower play drums at Altamont Park
summary: He heard her drum at an Altamont Park picnic; she had picked up sticks without study and was about five years younger.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Uh-huh. Well, I mean were there any bands that she was playing in at that time? 'Cause she must've talked to you, to tell you that she was a drummer, right? Was there any conversation like that?
Yeah, yeah. She talked with me.
And you had a chance to hear her, at that point?
No, I didn't have a chance to hear her.
When did you hear her?
I heard her when we started to playin' at a picnic, out at Altamont Park. Altamont Park.
Altamont?
Altamont Park. Altamont.
Altamont.
Yeah. That's when I heard her.
You heard her--was she playing with your group, or just happened to be playing with the band that you were with?
She had to come out there playing drums with the band that I was with.
Uh-huh.
And I was sittin' there playin', and I was surprised when she started to playin', you know.
Seeing a woman play like that, huh?
Yeah, and she could play so good. She could really play.
Yeah. At that time, I guess there weren't very many women playing drums?
No.
What about trumpets and saxophones? Did you know any?
trumpets. Drums,
No. No drums.
Yeah, it was later, I guess, when-- huh?
Just played drums. She could play a loud drum, too (chuckle). I remember---bumb-bum-bum-bum--she could go on the drum, I was thinkin' about it--when you came up, I was thinkin' about it.
About her?
Yeah.
Yeah. Well, I never got a chance to hear her play, but I'm pretty sure she was a fantastic--
No, you didn't get a chance to hear her play.
She inspired so many. What's that?
She inspired many a person.
Oh, yeah. That's why I was curious about Alton, who was her nephew, 'cause he was also a very active, good drummer.
Yeah, he was. He was a very good drummer.
Yes.
Was she older or younger than you?
Can we find out about her age, compared with yours?
Oh, yes. I was older than she was.
About what, eight? ten years? Do you have an idea?

Yeah, I was around (unintelligible) then I can tell you how old I was--'cause I'm pin this thing down. I was playin' and she was playin', too.--was playin' at the park. I can't think of the name of that park now. It's been so long, boy. But she was playin', all right.
Uh-huh. Do you have an idea how much older you might've been?
Than she?
Five years? Ten years? Do you have an idea?
Oh, about five years older than her.
You were about five years older than she was?
About five years. And if I think of it while we're talkin', if it comes to me, I'll tell you about it.
Okay.
She were a very good drummer, very good.
Uh-huh. Do you know anything about her studying? Did she study with anyone, or was she just (unintelligible) playing?
No, she didn't study with anyone. She just picked up the sticks and started playing, out at the park.
